steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 9x13-inch baking dish.

Slice potatoes with skins on into 1/4 inch thick slices. Place potatoes into a large pot and cover with salted water. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce heat to medium-low, cover and simmer until tender, 10 to 15 minutes. Drain and allow to steam dry for a minute or two.

Mix together mayonnaise, sour cream, onion powder, garlic powders, seasoned salt, pepper, bacon, onion, and American cheese in a bowl. Stir in potato slices. Pour mixture into prepared baking dish. Sprinkle top with grated Parmesan cheese.
Bake in the preheated oven until bubbly and beginning to brown, 35 to 40 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Scalloped Potatoes with Bacon
raw_recipe.description: Scalloped potatoes with bacon, sour cream, onions, and cheese make a tasty, hearty potato dish for dinner, picnics, or potlucks.

review.reviewBody: This is my recipe, so I wanted to be sure to tell people to leave the peels on the potatoes-it adds a great texture. Also, the potatoes should be the medium-sized reds Thanks so much and I hope you enjoy them!

While I found this slightly unappealing preparing (not sure why?) this was DELICIOUS!! I halved since it’s just two of us and used Colby vs American. Lessons learned when halving; boil time needs less, bake time is still about 30ish minutes. While a wonderful dish in its own rite, paired wonderfully with our steak dinner tonight. Will ABSOLUTELY make again! Thank you Megan J Crow!

Ok. Changes I made... partly due to what I had on hand and partly to the fact I can't stand to cook with mayonnaise. Used four mid-size russet potatoes and a whole yellow onion. Instead of mayo and sour cream, I used cream of chicken/mushroom soup and enough milk to make 12 oz. Also, used a full pack of cooked and well-drained bacon. There was a goof that turned out good... I used garlic powder, but messed up and grabbed garlic salt instead of onion powder. Ended up giving it the perfect amount of salt and I happen to really like garlic, so it was good! Will be making this again!

Absolutely fantastic! Made these for my boyfriend to take to “Friendsgiving” and they were the first thing gone. My potato hating man even devoured his helping! I (almost) doubled the sauce and used half sour cream/half French onion dip as suggested by other users and I really liked the blend. I also cut my potatoes a bit thicker so they could stand up to sitting in the fridge overnight. Love, love, love these potatoes and this recipe is now in permanent rotation.

This was great. I didn’t have red potatoes so I used Yukon gold and shredded cheddar. I used 1c sour cream to 1/2 cup mayonnaise because I prefer the sour cream. Didn’t have bacon but used ground beef. Husband loved it too. So it’s a win. Will do it again next time with a Mexican flair to it.

This is the best scalloped potato recipe I have ever made. I halved it since there are only two of us, and had to substitute three ingredients:
I used Cottage Cheese instead of sour cream.
I used processed cheese and Italian blend cheese.
I used yellow onion instead of red.

When I mixed it up, it was WAY to thick to 'stir in' the potatoes or to 'pour' into the baking dish; it was more the consistency of stiff bread dough, so I added a bit more cottage cheese and mayonnaise, and then added enough half-and-half to make it just a BIT thinner. Also, to keep them from breaking up in the still stiff mixture, I pulled the potatoes before they were completely tender and baked the finished dish a little longer to get them done.

The flavor was fantastic, and this is now MY scalloped potato recipe!!

Everyone including the five men at our table loved this recipe. I have since served it to others, and it is always a requested recipe. One change I made is to crumble bacon on top instead of incorporating into ingredients. This keeps bacon crisp with adds texture. FYI I have recently begun to try this with other recipes that use bacon, including baked beans. The difference is amazing as the bacon does not become soft but maintains the crunchy texture which is so appealing to the palate.

I'm not a fan of potatoes, but my husband definitely is. So I gave this recipe a whirl and loved it. First of all the recipe was scaled down to 3 servings, which was just right for the 2 of us, plus a serving of leftovers. I used Russets rather than red potatoes and cooked them until they were barely tender. I doubled the sauce and it was just right for the amount of potatoes and eye balled the amount of bacon, red onion, cheddar cheese, and parm. After 40 minutes in the oven, these potatoes were cooked to perfection, bubbly and a beautiful golden brown, not to mention down right tasty. This one's a keeper! Thanks for sharing your recipe Old Crow.

Very good. I forgot to add the sour cream! I added milk to the sauce to make it creamier and easier to spread. Then I figured out Why i had to do that- forgot the sour cream! That being said and sans sour cream these came out great. Doubled the recipe and assembled it a day ahead of time and baked before serving.

This recipe is a keeper. I used medium cheddar instead of American cheese as that's what I had. White onion ditto. I diced the bacon, fried it, and when it was almost done I sauteed the onion in with the bacon. The salt will be cut back a bit next time, but other than that, it's good as is.

I took a half cup of mayonnaise and 1 cup of sour cream and added the garlic and onion powders, seasoned salt and the pepper and stirred up all together. I spooned a layer of that "sauce" into the bottom of my baking dish followed by a layer of potatoes. Then I sprinkled a layer of cheese, then crumbled up bacon and then some sliced green onions. Then I spooned more "sauce", a layer of potatoes and then cheese. Then I added some grated Parmesan and then a layer of bacon and finally some green onions again. It's now one of our families favorite dishes!
Only change I make is adding in some diced ham, but this is a wonderful, although very rich, recipe.
These are not scalloped potatoes. These are Au gratin potatoes because of the cheese.

Very tasty and the Fam loved it! Being an old school cook, recipes are usually just a basic guide for me and I rarely measure ingredients. This guide was a real winner in my house. I did not include the bacon as I was making this as a side for a baked ham and left some of the peel as the author suggested (its always my favorite part of most potatoes). Next time I will include the bacon just to see how it differs. My wife is a chef from Mexico City that does not care for most southern dishes like stuffing or greens. But my Mexicana could not get enough of this. I know if I promise to prepare this for dinner she will let me cook more often!

My husband fought me on these, saying he didn't like scalloped potatoes. Boy did he change his tune! These are delicious. I was raised on Miracle Whip, so I used that instead of mayo. It gave a flavorful tang to the dish. I also used a TBSP of minced garlic, rather than the onion, and extra sharp cheddar instead of American cheese. This recipe is a keeper!
I added a cup of milk and some cornstarch. This is now our favourite scallop potato recipe.
I baked this in my smoker and it turned out great
Wonderful recipe I make it as written only omitting the seasoning salt. Great leftover too. Everyone LOVES it.
